transcript_text:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-10
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Mark Davis (Crestpoint - Head of InfoSec), Sana Patel (Procurement), Ethan Moore (Cloud Architect)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Redwood walked through key SIG/CAIQ controls and evidence mapping. Discussed SOC 2/ISO posture, RBAC/SSO via SAML/IdP, audit log retention and access, data residency options (regions and VPC/private deployments), and encryption/KMS integration. Customer requested redacted SOC2, example audit logs, and a populated SIG spreadsheet with evidence links. Next steps agreed: Redwood to send artifacts and schedule KMS deep-dive.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex Chen from Redwood, AE. With me is Priya Rao, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Mark Davis: Good, thanks. Mark here. We wanted to run through the SIG questionnaire — we've got a long vendor process and some tight timelines.
[00:15] Alex Chen: Totally. We'll go section by section and flag where we can provide evidence, where we need a statement, and where there's a configuration on your side. Note: we uploaded a starter SIG spreadsheet and a link to our SOC artifacts in the invite.
[00:25] Sana Patel: Yep we saw the invite, but procurement asked for a walkthrough so we understand what you'll actually provide as evidence versus what is our integration work.
[00:32] Priya Rao: Great. High level first — Redwood is SOC 2 Type II for the control scope around hosted inference. We also maintain ISO 27001 in our broader org. We can provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II report and a controls matrix. The SOC report is usually redacted to remove customer names and a few infra details.
[00:45] Mark Davis: Good. For Crestpoint we also need audit logs to prove separation of duties and admin access. Can you provide sample audit logs or a schema?
[00:52] Priya Rao: Yes, we can share sanitized sample logs. They include timestamp, actor, action, resource, outcome. We'll redact any customer PII. We also have a logging retention policy — 1 year by default for hosted, with add-on retention available.
[01:05] Ethan Moore: Quick question on network: are we talking VPC peering or Private deployment? We have strict controls and prefer no public egress for some workloads.
[01:12] Alex Chen: We support multiple modes. For most customers you can go with Dedicated or Private deployments. Dedicated gives committed GPU pools in a customer-dedicated tenancy. Private provides a VPC-friendly control plane and can be run in a customer-managed VPC or on-prem. We'll map the SIG responses accordingly.
[01:25] Mark Davis: For the SIG, question about encryption at rest and KMS: do you manage keys or can we integrate our KMS?
[01:32] Priya Rao: Both. By default we manage encryption keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) but we support customer-managed keys through KMS integration and HSM in private deployments. One caveat — in hosted mode, bringing your own key is available via our enterprise contract and requires an onboarding runbook.
[01:45] Mark Davis: Right. We'll likely require customer-managed keys for certain datasets.
[01:48] Priya Rao: Noted. We'll flag that in the SIG answer as "supported — requires enterprise contract and KMS configuration."
[01:55] Sana Patel: On SSO and RBAC, Crestpoint uses Okta and enforces SCIM for provisioning. Do you support SCIM and SAML?
[02:02] Alex Chen: Yes, SAML + SCIM are supported. Role-based access is configurable via our Console; you can map Okta groups to Redwood roles. Priya, want to show the quick RBAC map?
[02:10] Priya Rao: Sure. (brief pause) So the Console has role templates: Admin, Developer, Auditor. SCIM syncs groups; permissions are enforced at the route/model level. One limitation to call out — in Dedicated older versions we had a small gap where custom roles required manual mapping; that's been resolved in our current platform release, but some docs may reference the older flow.
[02:30] Mark Davis: Ok, we need an auditor role that can see logs but not data. Is that available?
[02:34] Priya Rao: Yes, Auditor role can view activity logs, billing, and audit trails but cannot invoke model endpoints or access raw prompt/response payloads. We'll include that mapping in the SIG evidence.
[02:46] Ethan Moore: About audit logs — do you capture request/response payloads? We can't have full user prompts retained for regulated workloads.
[02:53] Priya Rao: Good question. By default we store metadata and trace logs; we persist full request/response only if customer opts-in for debugging. For customers with stricter privacy we can disable payload retention and enable only metadata plus hashed indicators for QA. That configuration is available both in Dedicated and Private. We'll note that in the SIG.
[03:10] Mark Davis: Data residency — we need deployments and logs to stay in us-east-1 for this initial pilot. Is that possible?
[03:16] Alex Chen: Yes, we have region controls. Hosted customers can choose region (US, EU, APAC) and Dedicated/Private can be constrained to specific regions or on-prem. For audit evidence we can produce a data residency statement and tag the controls that are region-dependent.
[03:30] Sana Patel: For the SIG there's a question about vendor penetration testing results and bug bounty. Do you have a regular pentest and program?
[03:37] Priya Rao: We run annual third-party pentests and have a coordinated disclosure process. We publish summaries internally and can provide a redacted pentest summary and our vuln management process as evidence. For more detail on active bug bounty, we rely on private programs and select partners — we can provide the program overview.
[03:52] Mark Davis: Competitors sometimes claim they have a continuous fuzzing pipeline. Do you do continuous sec testing?
[03:58] Priya Rao: We do automated security scans and CI/CD-integrated checks, along with scheduled dynamic tests. For customers that require it we can reference our DevSecOps pipeline description.
[04:08] Alex Chen: Quick note on the SIG itself — there are a few questions that are "config only" versus "evidence". For example, if the SIG asks whether we support SAML, that's a simple "Yes with doc link." If it asks for proof of user provisioning, that's where we'll attach SCIM logs and a provisioning runbook. We'll mark each control as either doc, config, or evidence.
[04:26] Mark Davis: Sounds sensible. For legal/procurement we need to see retention periods and deletion procedures. Can you share your data deletion SLA?
[04:33] Priya Rao: Yes — we have a documented data retention and deletion policy. Deletion requests for customer data in hosted are processed within 30 days typically; for Dedicated/Private we provide procedures to run deletion in customer environment. We'll include a link to the policy and an excerpt in the SIG doc.
[04:47] Ethan Moore: On network egress and allowlists — can we have dedicated NAT or egress controls?
[04:52] Alex Chen: In Private deployments you control the VPC egress. In Dedicated we offer allowlist IP ranges and peering options. For the SIG we'll indicate which controls are available per deployment model.
[05:03] Sana Patel: There's a SIG question about subcontractors and third-party services — do you use any external cloud vendors or analytics vendors that touch logs?
[05:10] Priya Rao: We use cloud providers (AWS/GCP) and a small set of vendor services for observability. We keep a vendor inventory and can provide a summary of subprocessors; for any sensitive item we can provide contracts and DPA info.
[05:22] Mark Davis: Great. Are there parts of the SIG you expect us to fill in or provide input on?
[05:27] Alex Chen: Yes, network diagrams and the list of systems that will integrate with Redwood endpoints — that's on your side. We'll ask for a short integration spreadsheet so we can map controls to Crestpoint's architecture.
[05:36] Ethan Moore: We'll prepare that. One more thing — latency SLA. The SIG has a performance/availability section — do you have an SLA we can reference?
[05:44] Alex Chen: We have SLA tiers for Dedicated customers. Hosted has published latency percentiles in our perf docs but SLA-backed uptime is part of Dedicated/enterprise contracts. We'll attach the SLA doc link and call out the differences in the SIG.
[05:56] Priya Rao: Back to encryption: for KMS integration there are a couple of implementation notes — key rotation cadence, access controls on KMS keys, and how we handle envelope encryption. We'll capture those steps in a short runbook and include config screenshots for the SIG.
[06:12] Mark Davis: Ok will need that runbook. Also, for evidence, do you provide screenshots or logged API calls for who rotated keys and when?
[06:19] Priya Rao: Yes — KMS access is logged in the cloud provider audit logs and we can include redacted examples showing key access events.
[06:27] Sana Patel: Procurement also asks for a sample contract clause around data ownership and liability. Do you have standard language?
[06:33] Alex Chen: We have a standard DPA and data ownership clause in our contracts; legal can provide language. I'll coordinate with your procurement team after this call.
[06:40] Mark Davis: Good. Can we also get an example of your audit trail query so our auditors can validate?
[06:46] Priya Rao: We'll include an example ELK/Kusto query or BigQuery example depending on your stack — sample queries for extracting admin actions, failed logins, and config changes.
[06:56] Alex Chen: We're about half-way through the SIG. Priya, do you want to call out the high-risk items we should escalate?
[07:02] Priya Rao: Sure — items to escalate: customer-managed KMS (setup onboarding), VPC/private deployment network constraints, and payload retention preferences. Those typically require architecture sessions and timeline alignment.
[07:14] Mark Davis: Timeline — we need vendor sign-off within three weeks. Can Redwood turn around the artifacts that quickly?
[07:20] Alex Chen: Yes, if we get the integration spreadsheet and clarify KMS needs we'll prioritize the artefacts. The SOC2 and pentest redactions are typically ready in 3 business days after request, SIG population within 2-3 business days.
[07:33] Ethan Moore: That's tight but doable. We'll aim to get the integration sheet to you tomorrow.
[07:37] Sana Patel: Procurement also needs a contact for contract negotiation.
[07:40] Alex Chen: That's me. I'll loop in our legal contact via email after this.
[07:45] (background noise, brief cross-talk)
[07:55] Priya Rao: Quick demo note — in the SIG there's a question on separation of duties for model updates. Our model rollout process includes canaries, A/B testing, and automatic fallback. We keep rollouts auditable and log the change events. We'll show the rollout audit examples in the evidence package.
[08:12] Mark Davis: Perfect. For the evidence links, can you provide a link to a view-only SIG spreadsheet?
[08:17] Alex Chen: Yes, we'll share a view-only link. Priya will own the sheet population.
[08:22] Priya Rao: I'll populate items marked as "fully controlled by Redwood" with document links, and mark items that require Crestpoint input with a note.
[08:30] Mark Davis: Any blockers on our side we should be aware of?
[08:35] Priya Rao: No blockers, just clarity on KMS and whether you'll require an on-prem Private deployment for the pilot. If it's on-prem, timelines for provisioning will be longer.
[08:46] Ethan Moore: For now pilot in us-east-1 hosted but with customer-managed key requirement. We'll confirm in the integration spreadsheet.
[08:54] Alex Chen: Great. Quick run-through of next steps before we close out.
[09:00] Alex Chen: Action items: I'll send redacted SOC2, pentest summary, and controls matrix; Priya will populate SIG spreadsheet and share view-only link; we'll schedule a KMS technical deep-dive next week. Any additional asks?
[09:12] Mark Davis: Can you also include sample sanitized audit logs and KMS access event examples?
[09:17] Priya Rao: Yes, included in my action items.
[09:20] Sana Patel: Procurement will wait for your contract contact and the DPA language.
[09:24] Alex Chen: I'll include legal contact in the follow-up email.
[09:28] (multiple participants): Thanks, thanks everyone.

Recap / Next steps (as discussed):
- Redwood to send redacted SOC 2 Type II report, controls matrix, redacted pentest summary, and sample sanitized audit logs. Link to SOC artifacts and SIG starter sheet will be provided.
- Priya to populate SIG spreadsheet with evidence links and mark items needing Crestpoint input; share view-only link by 2026-04-14.
- Schedule KMS integration deep-dive (suggested 2026-04-20) to discuss BYOK onboarding and key rotation.
- Crestpoint to provide integration spreadsheet listing systems that will call Redwood endpoints (due 2026-04-11).

References / shared artifacts mentioned:
- SIG starter spreadsheet (view-only link to be provided)
- SOC2_redacted.pdf (redwood-link or s3 link)
- KMS onboarding runbook (internal link)
- Rollout audit examples (screenshots and query snippets)

End of transcript.
